recipeCards.title: Margin Note Market Revision Recipe
recipeCards.useCase: Adult-led, screen-free, printable paper recipe card for older writers to turn a broad draft note into one precise table revision.
recipeCards.adultSetup: Print the card, place paper and pencils on the table, and invite the writer to imagine a quiet market stall that trades only kind notes and clearer words.
recipeCards.kidDirection: Choose one draft idea, imagine it as a note from Margin Note Market, and revise the idea so a reader can picture the exact story change.
recipeCards.recipeTitlePrompt: Recipe title: My margin-note story recipe is called ____________________.
recipeCards.storyIngredientsPrompt: Story ingredients: I need one fuzzy draft note ____________________, one exact replacement word ____________________, and one kind question ____________________.
recipeCards.mixItUpPrompt: Mix-it-up note: Change the broad note into a clear action the writer can try next: ____________________.
recipeCards.servingSentencePath: Serving sentence path: The note first says ____________________; the writer looks closer at ____________________; the revised line becomes ____________________.
recipeCards.revisionNudge: Revision nudge: Replace one vague word with a specific table, paper, pencil, or sketch detail: ____________________.
recipeCards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Work silently and revise only one sentence from the card: ____________________.
recipeCards.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: Use this margin note later to improve a tiny story about ____________________.

recipeCards.title: Binding Day Boardwalk Sequence Recipe
recipeCards.useCase: Adult-led, screen-free, printable paper recipe card for arranging a short story into a clear beginning, turn, and ending.
recipeCards.adultSetup: Print the card, set out paper and pencils, and ask the writer to imagine a boardwalk where paper pages line up in the right order.
recipeCards.kidDirection: Imagine three boardwalk stops, sketch one small page clue, and write the order that helps the story feel finished.
recipeCards.recipeTitlePrompt: Recipe title: My Binding Day sequence recipe is called ____________________.
recipeCards.storyIngredientsPrompt: Story ingredients: I need an opening page clue ____________________, a middle turn ____________________, and a final boardwalk detail ____________________.
recipeCards.mixItUpPrompt: Mix-it-up note: Move one event earlier or later so the story order makes better sense: ____________________.
recipeCards.servingSentencePath: Serving sentence path: First the paper page shows ____________________; next the boardwalk turn reveals ____________________; finally the ending lands on ____________________.
recipeCards.revisionNudge: Revision nudge: Add one bridge sentence between two story moments: ____________________.
recipeCards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Number three paper ideas, then write only the middle turn here: ____________________.
recipeCards.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: Use the final boardwalk detail to start a short scene about ____________________.

recipeCards.title: Index Card Theater Character Recipe
recipeCards.useCase: Adult-led, screen-free, printable paper recipe card for building a character choice through two short lines and one stage cue.
recipeCards.adultSetup: Print the card, place paper and pencils on the table, and invite the writer to imagine a tiny theater made from index cards and sketched signs.
recipeCards.kidDirection: Give a character one clear want, sketch a simple stage cue, and write two lines that show the choice changing.
recipeCards.recipeTitlePrompt: Recipe title: My index-card character recipe is called ____________________.
recipeCards.storyIngredientsPrompt: Story ingredients: I need a character who wants ____________________, a table-stage cue ____________________, and a choice that changes ____________________.
recipeCards.mixItUpPrompt: Mix-it-up note: Swap the first line or reply so the character choice becomes clearer: ____________________.
recipeCards.servingSentencePath: Serving sentence path: The character expects ____________________; the stage cue shows ____________________; the choice turns toward ____________________.
recipeCards.revisionNudge: Revision nudge: Add one visible action that shows the character choice without explaining it: ____________________.
recipeCards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Write only the two spoken lines on the paper card: ____________________.
recipeCards.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: Use the clearest character choice to begin a table scene about ____________________.

recipeCards.title: Clue Label Tower Sensory Recipe
recipeCards.useCase: Adult-led, screen-free, printable paper recipe card for choosing precise sound, color, texture, and shape clues for a short museum scene.
recipeCards.adultSetup: Print the card, set paper and pencils on the table, and ask the writer to imagine a quiet tower museum with labels for ordinary story clues.
recipeCards.kidDirection: Pick one imagined exhibit, sketch its label, and use concrete sensory words to make the setting easy to picture.
recipeCards.recipeTitlePrompt: Recipe title: My clue-label sensory recipe is called ____________________.
recipeCards.storyIngredientsPrompt: Story ingredients: I need one exhibit shape ____________________, one color clue ____________________, one texture word ____________________, and one quiet sound ____________________.
recipeCards.mixItUpPrompt: Mix-it-up note: Trade one general description for a more concrete museum-label clue: ____________________.
recipeCards.servingSentencePath: Serving sentence path: The tower label names ____________________; the setting feels ____________________; the clue points the reader toward ____________________.
recipeCards.revisionNudge: Revision nudge: Replace a plain describing word with one sensory detail from the label: ____________________.
recipeCards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Sketch the exhibit label first, then write one sensory sentence: ____________________.
recipeCards.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: Use this label later to build a quiet museum scene about ____________________.

recipeCards.title: Revision River Ferry Ending Recipe
recipeCards.useCase: Adult-led, screen-free, printable paper recipe card for polishing a short ending by echoing one earlier story clue.
recipeCards.adultSetup: Print the card, place paper and pencils on the table, and invite the writer to imagine a calm ferry carrying draft sentences across Revision River.
recipeCards.kidDirection: Choose one earlier clue, draft an ending, and revise the final sentence so the ending feels connected.
recipeCards.recipeTitlePrompt: Recipe title: My Revision River ending recipe is called ____________________.
recipeCards.storyIngredientsPrompt: Story ingredients: I need one earlier clue ____________________, one ferry crossing image ____________________, and one final feeling ____________________.
recipeCards.mixItUpPrompt: Mix-it-up note: Bring back one clue from the beginning so the ending feels complete: ____________________.
recipeCards.servingSentencePath: Serving sentence path: At first the story notices ____________________; near the river the clue returns as ____________________; the final sentence becomes ____________________.
recipeCards.revisionNudge: Revision nudge: Trim one extra phrase or add one clearer ending image: ____________________.
recipeCards.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: Circle the ending sentence on paper and write the revised version here: ____________________.
recipeCards.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: Use this revised ending to finish a tiny story about ____________________.
